Get started with GICHighDimension

Source: vignettes/GICHighDimension.Rmd
GICHighDimension.Rmd

GICHighDimension selects variables in high-dimensional regression by maximizing a generalized information criterion (GIC). The search is a Hopfield-network style coordinate search: it visits the candidate variables in random order, proposes adding a variable that is out of the model or removing one that is in it, and keeps the move when the criterion improves. The method is described in Xiao and Walker (2026), Statistics and Computing, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11222-026-10853-5.

Setting up Julia

The search runs in ‘Julia’ (≥ 1.9). Install Julia from https://julialang.org/downloads/, then connect R to it:

library(GICHighDimension)
setup_julia()               # or setup_julia("/path/to/julia/bin")
install_julia_packages()    # first time only

Selecting variables

Simulate a sparse linear model with 30 candidate predictors, 3 of them active:

set.seed(123)
n <- 300; p <- 30
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)
beta <- c(2, -1.5, 1, rep(0, p - 3))
Y <- LP_to_Y(X, beta, family = "Normal")

Run the search with EBIC, starting from the first five variables:

fit <- GICSelection(
  X, Y,
  Initial_Column      = 1:5,
  Calculate_GIC       = "Calculate_EBIC",
  Calculate_GIC_short = "Calculate_EBIC_short",
  k    = 15,     # skip models with 15 or more variables
  Nsim = 3       # passes over the variables
)

sort(fit$selected_coeffs[[length(fit$selected_coeffs)]])
#> [1] 1 2 3

fit$GIC_values records the criterion after each of the Nsim * p steps, so plot(fit$GIC_values, type = "l") shows the search converging. Models never have more than min(k, n) - 1 variables.

Choosing a criterion

Every criterion has the form GIC=Y⊤HYn−Kσ̂2ncn, \mathrm{GIC} = \frac{Y^\top H Y}{n} - \frac{K\,\hat\sigma^2}{n}\,c_n , where HH is the hat matrix of the selected columns, KK the number of selected variables, σ̂2\hat\sigma^2 the residual variance, and cnc_n the penalty:

Function Penalty cnc_n
Calculate_AIC 11
Calculate_BIC log⁡n\log n
Calculate_SIC n\sqrt n
Calculate_CAIC 1+log⁡n1 + \log n
Calculate_GIC2 P1/3P^{1/3}
Calculate_GIC3 2log⁡P2 \log P
Calculate_GIC4 2(log⁡P+log⁡log⁡P)2(\log P + \log\log P)
Calculate_GIC5 log⁡log⁡nlog⁡P\log\log n \, \log P
Calculate_GIC6 log⁡nlog⁡P\log n \, \log P
Calculate_EBIC log⁡n+γlog⁡(PK)\log n + \gamma \log \binom{P}{K}, with γ=0.6\gamma = 0.6 by default

Here PP is the number of candidate variables. Calculate_AICc, Calculate_CAICF and Calculate_AttIC use slightly different forms; see ?information_criteria. Pass the name of a criterion and of its _short version to GICSelection(). For EBIC, change γ\gamma with the gamma argument.

Other response types

For a matrix response (several outcomes sharing the same predictors), pass an n×qn \times q matrix as Y; the criterion is then the trace of a q×qq \times q matrix.

For a non-Gaussian response, transform it to the linear-predictor scale with Y_to_LP() before selecting, and estimate the coefficients of the selected model with Beta_estimate():

y_count <- LP_to_Y(X, beta / 2, family = "Poisson")
fit_pois <- GICSelection(X, Y_to_LP(y_count, family = "Poisson"), 1:5,
                         "Calculate_EBIC", "Calculate_EBIC_short", k = 15, Nsim = 3)
selected <- sort(fit_pois$selected_coeffs[[length(fit_pois$selected_coeffs)]])
Beta_estimate(X[, selected, drop = FALSE], y_count, family = "Poisson")

The supported families are Normal, Bernoulli, Binomial, Poisson, Gamma, Exponential, InverseGaussian, NegativeBinomial, Geometric, MultivariateNormal and Multinomial.
